title: ADVANCED COATINGS AND MATERIALS FOR LOW EARTH ORBIT SATELLITES FOR DARK AND QUIET SKIES EXPRO PLUS
description: Objective: To develop advanced coatings and materials for Dark and Quiet Skies (DQS) with optimised reflectance/scattering, scalable production, and durability in (V)LEO environments.Description: The expansion of satellite mega constellations in (Very) Low Earth Orbit ((V)LEO) for Telecommunications or Earth Observation applications poses growing challenges for astronomy, particularly due to increased satellite brightness and stray light. Key contributors to this issue are large external spacecraft surfacessuch as solar arrays, radiators, multilayer insulation (MLI), optical instruments, and structural componentsthat reflect sunlight and increaseoptical interference. Traditionally, spacecraft materials have been optimized for thermal, mechanical, or electrical properties, with limited consideration for optical performance in the visible range. This activity aims to identify high-risk materials and applications that conflict with Dark and Quiet Skies (DQS) guidelines, especially where qualified low-impact alternatives are lacking. Based on this evaluation, the focus will shift to developing new coatings or materials that reduce optical interference while preserving existing performance standards. Scalability and compatibility with complex satellite designs is to be considered. Two specific applications are aimed to be addressed: 1. A high-risk material or application identified during the initial assessment (e.g., solar cells, MLI, thrusters). 2. Large deployable radiators, whose surfaces contribute significantly to spacecraft brightness. Here, innovative microstructured surfaces will be designed to reflect sunlight at controlled angles away from Earth and be coated to match the optical performance of existing OSR or SSM materials. This activity involves the development, testing, and characterization of new materials with a focus on critical optical properties such as Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Function (BRDF), Total IntegratedScatter (TIS), and total hemispherical reflectance, in addition to standard performance metrics. This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review of current materials and available alternatives - Development of DQS mitigation strategies - Selection of twodetailed application cases - Definition of requirements and material/coating design - Sample manufacturing - Testing of new materials for both cases including mechanical stress and micrometeoroid impact assessments

title: 13679 Biotoptypenkartierung zur Neuabgrenzung des LSG, u. a. durch Fernerkundung, Datenauswertung
description: Der Kreis Gütersloh beabsichtigt, auf den Flächen außerhalb der Geltungsbereiche von Land-schaftsplänen die veraltete Landschaftsschutzgebietsverordnung (LSG-VO) zu überarbeiten. Ziel der Biotoptypenkartierung ist es, eine fachliche Grundlage und erste Einschätzung der Landschaftsstruktur für die Bearbeitung der Abgrenzung des Landschaftsschutzgebietses zu erhalten. Das Plangebiet erstreckt sich über die Kommunen Versmold, Harsewinkel, Herzebrock-Clarholz, Rheda-Wiedenbrück, Langenberg, Rietberg und Verl (tlw) ohne die Ortslagen und ohne die bestehenden Naturschutzgebiete. Das Plangebiet hat eine Größe von ca. 47.460 ha. Die Bearbeitungs- und Unterscheidungstiefe soll an den Kartierschlüssel für die Eingriffsregelung in NRW angelehnt werden, die Biotoptypen sind auf der Ebene der Biotopgruppen (gekennzeichnet durch 2 Großbuchstaben) zu unterscheiden. 13679 Biotoptypenkartierung zur Neuabgrenzung des LSG, u. a. durch Fernerkundung, Datenauswertung

title: Lunar i-hab –  Test Facility ITT
description:
The Cislunar Gateway – International Habitat (Lunar I-HAB) is ESA’s contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2028. The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a ‘basecamp’ for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the Contractor for the Test Facility Services, to be supplied in the framework of the I-Hab environmental test campaign, and for the procurement of the Mechanical Test Adapter.
During this test campaign, I-Hab will undergo two main environmental tests, sinusoidal and acoustic vibrations, and several other mechanical, fluidic and functional verifications. The Contractor is requested to provide all support services, facilities, equipment, material, personnel and documentation needed to perform or support the activities specified in ITT data package 
Moreover, the Contractor is responsible for the procurement of the Mechanical Test Adapter (MTA), the GSE used as interface between I-Hab and relevant test machines and facilities.

Further information concerning the Cislunar Gateway and the ESA contributions can be found on the Agency’s website here:https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon
